title: Epimorphism and final object
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category. A morphism $f:X\to Y$ of $\mathcal C$ is an *epimorphism* if for every object $W$ and every pair of morphisms $a,b:Y\to W$ with $a\circ f=b\circ f$ one has $a=b$. An object $Z$ of $\mathcal C$ is *final* if for every object $Y$ of $\mathcal C$ there is exactly one morphism $Y\to Z$; equivalently, $Z$ is a limit of the empty diagram (the empty product).
